- src/maintenance/detect.ts - export function detectStaleAnnotations(codebasePath: string): string[] - JSDoc: - @story docs/stories/009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS.story.md - @req REQ-MAINT-DETECT - Behavior: - Resolves workspaceRoot = path.resolve(process.cwd(), codebasePath). - If workspaceRoot does not exist or is not a directory: returns []. - Uses getAllFiles(workspaceRoot) to gather all files. - For each file, processFileForStaleAnnotations reads content (with try/catch; read errors are ignored) and scans for @story using regex /@story\s+([^\s]+)/g. - For each match, handleStoryMatch: - Skips unsafe paths via isUnsafeStoryPath(storyPath) (avoids traversal, absolute paths, invalid extensions) before any fs/stat operations. - Computes project and codebase candidates via path.resolve and applies enforceProjectBoundary for each. - Collects only in-project candidates; if none, returns (does not mark stale). - Checks existence only for in-project candidates via anyInProjectCandidateExists; if none exist, adds storyPath to `stale` Set. - Returns Array.from(stale) (list of stale story references).
- src/maintenance/update.ts - export function updateAnnotationReferences(codebasePath: string, oldPath: string, newPath: string): number - JSDoc: - @story docs/stories/009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS.story.md - @req REQ-MAINT-UPDATE - Behavior: - Validates that codebasePath exists and is a directory; otherwise returns 0 (safe no-op). - Escapes oldPath for use in regex; builds regex `(@story\\s*)${escapedOldPath}`. - Uses getAllFiles(codebasePath) to list files. - For each file, processFileForAnnotationUpdates: - Skips non-regular files (stat.isFile() check). - Reads content, performs content.replace(regex, (match, p1) => `${p1}${newPath}`) while incrementing replacementCountRef.count. - Writes file back only if newContent !== content. - Returns total replacementCountRef.count, indicating how many annotations were updated.
- src/maintenance/batch.ts - export function batchUpdateAnnotations(codebasePath: string, mappings: { oldPath: string; newPath: string }[]): number - JSDoc: @story 009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS, @req REQ-MAINT-BATCH, REQ-MAINT-VERIFY. - Loops over mappings, summing results of updateAnnotationReferences; supports batch updates across many references. - export function verifyAnnotations(codebasePath: string): boolean - JSDoc: @story 009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS, @req REQ-MAINT-VERIFY. - Returns detectStaleAnnotations(codebasePath).length === 0 (true if no stale references).

- src/maintenance/utils.ts - export function getAllFiles(dir: string): string[] - Validates directory exists and is a directory; otherwise returns []. - Uses traverseDirectory to recursively iterate entries, recursing into directories and pushing only regular files to the list. - Shared by detect/update/batch, ensuring consistent traversal and minimal side effects.
Maintenance CLI implementation (src/maintenance/cli.ts): - JSDoc references story 009 and maps to REQ-MAINT-* entries. - Key pieces: - ParsedCliInput, ParsedFlags data structures. - parseCliInput(rawArgv): extracts command and args from process.argv-like array. - createDefaultFlags(): defaults { root: process.cwd(), json: false }. - applyFlag(flags, args, index): handles --root, --json, --format (text|json), --from, --to, --dry-run; invalid format throws Error. - parseFlags(args): iterates args using applyFlag. - runMaintenanceCli(rawArgv): - Parses command; if missing/-h/--help: prints help and returns EXIT_OK. - Switches on command: detect/verify/report/update; unknown -> error + help + EXIT_USAGE. - Wraps dispatch in try/catch and on error logs `traceability-maint failed: ...` and returns EXIT_USAGE, meeting REQ-MAINT-SAFE. - handleDetect(args): - Uses parseFlags; calls detectStaleAnnotations(root). - If flags.json: logs JSON.stringify({ root, stale }). - Else: logs either "No stale @story annotations found." or each stale story, plus a summary line and hint to run `traceability-maint report`. - Returns EXIT_OK when no stale, EXIT_STALE when there are stale references. - handleVerify(args): - Uses verifyAnnotations(root); logs success message and returns EXIT_OK if true, else logs guidance and returns EXIT_STALE. - handleReport(args): - Uses generateMaintenanceReport(root) and chosen format (default text; optionally json). - If json: logs JSON.stringify({ root, report }). - Else: logs a markdown-style header and report content, or a "No stale... Nothing to report." message if empty. - Returns EXIT_OK. - handleUpdate(args): - Requires flags.from and flags.to; if missing, logs error, prints help, returns EXIT_USAGE (2). - For dry-run: - Uses generateMaintenanceReport(root) to estimate potential impact (estimatedStaleCount). - Logs human-readable summary or JSON payload { mode: "dry-run", root, from, to, estimatedStaleCount }. - Does not modify any files; exits EXIT_OK. - For actual update: - Calls updateAnnotationReferences(root, from, to) to perform replacements. - Logs a summary of updated count (with correct pluralization), or JSON payload { root, from, to, updated: count }. - Returns EXIT_OK. - printHelp(): prints full CLI help including all commands and options. - if (require.main === module) process.exit(runMaintenanceCli(process.argv)); connects Node CLI entry point.

traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria for docs/stories/009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS.story.md are satisfied by the current implementation:
- Core Functionality: Implemented in src/maintenance/detect.ts, update.ts, batch.ts, report.ts and wired through src/maintenance/index.ts and src/maintenance/cli.ts. Tools detect stale @story references, update them (including batch mappings), verify annotations via re-checking for staleness, and generate reports (text/JSON) summarizing work. - Quality Standards: Maintenance operations reuse shared traversal utilities (getAllFiles), perform minimal, targeted string replacements on @story annotations, validate directories before traversing, and write files only when content changes, preserving the rest of the code and formatting. - Integration: Maintenance tools are exposed: - As a dedicated Node CLI (`traceability-maint`) via package.json bin mapping. - As a programmatic API under the plugin’s `maintenance` export in src/index.ts. They leverage existing story reference utilities (storyReferenceUtils) for boundary and safety checks, aligning with earlier validation stories. - User Experience: The CLI provides clear subcommands (detect, verify, report, update), helpful messages, structured reports, JSON modes for automation, explicit exit codes (0 for success, 1 for stale/invalid, 2 for usage errors), and a comprehensive help/usage output. - Error Handling: The implementation handles non-existent directories, unreadable files, invalid format flags, missing parameters for update, permission issues, and unsafe story paths. Error paths are either caught at the CLI boundary (with friendly messages and EXIT_USAGE) or are explicitly exercised in tests (e.g., permission-denied case in detect-isolated). Security-focused tests verify that no filesystem checks occur for unsafe or out-of-project paths. - Documentation: The Maintenance CLI has a dedicated section in README.md with explanations and concrete examples, plus a pointer to a detailed API reference. This aligns with the story’s documentation acceptance criterion.
Given the direct traceability between requirements, implementation, and tests, and the absence of uncovered or unimplemented REQ-* items for this story, the status is PASSED.
